title: How did I do? #theatre #michellewilliams #broadway #review #annachris...
transcript: So when a theater production inspires a passionate negative response from me, I try to be honest about my feelings as someone who reviews shows on here, but I also strive to keep things respectful, constructive and classy. And I'll let you interpret that how you will as I talk about Oscar nominee Michelle Williams starring in this revival of Eugenia Nielsen's Pulitzer winning play on a Christie, directed by her husband, Thomas Kale. In that same spirit, I do have one positive thing to say about this production, which was that it was pretty well crafted from like a staging and design standpoint, including original incidental music by Oscar nominated film composer Nicholas Britell, which was a fun surprise. But I will say pretty much nothing else about it worked for me. Starting off with a couple more surface level things, I guess. First of all, the character of Anna Christie is canonically, textually 20 years old. And I would say that is reflected in how she behaves and what she does. Meanwhile, Michelle Williams is 45 years old and she looks it. And that's not an insult. Nothing wrong with being 45. But I would say there's a pretty clear disconnect here between the performance and the character as written. Secondly, there's a lot of accent work and dialect work throughout this production that is, let's say, quite adventurous. And not only did I have trouble understanding a lot of the words in this production, I think it Pulled focus even on a deeper level. In fact, in multiple ways, the acting and the direction of the actors was, I would say, doing too much. It felt very overwrought to me. If you ever went to acting school, do you remember the exercises that the teachers would do to help build out the voice, physicality and behavioral traits of the character, like picking an animal to emulate, stuff like that, potentially a very useful tool in the actor's tool belt. But I got the sense that that sort of character work was the primary focus of this creative process in a way that allowed much more important things to fall by the wayside. Like they were putting so much energy into flexing their extensive individual character work that things like chemistry, relationship building and listening and responding were not sufficiently present here. Even some of the more broad strokes directorial things like the exploration of themes, the arc, the sense of forward progression felt deprioritized here in a conspicuous way that even some pretty lighting and staging couldn't overcome. And that lack of coherence and connective tissue in the storytelling made it so that even when they were making choices that elicited multiple types of strong reactions from me, I was simultaneously struggling to stay engaged with the contents of the play. And I think I'm gonna stop there.
